newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Petkoff rules out 1998 election bid.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Petkoff rules out 1998 election bid.

text.p: Venezuela's ebullient Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff ruled out Tuesday suggestions he might stand for president in 1998 national elections.
"I have systematically told those who ask me that it (the presidency) does not interest me," Petkoff told local Union Radio in an interview.

Petkoff, who fought as a communist guerrilla against the government in the 1960s, has been one of the most prominent members of the government since joining President Rafael Caldera's cabinet in March 1996.
Petkoff's role as the main spokesman of an economic reform program launched in April last year has won him plaudits abroad and seen him become the most popular member of Caldera's government.
The 65-year-old Movement to Socialism (MAS) party founder has made two unsuccessful bids for the presidency.
"I've paid that military service. I was a candidate twice and that's enough," he said.
